key_findings.finding: The deformity is boutonnière deformity—not mallet, swan-neck, hammer, or lumbrical-plus. Its characteristic extensor-mechanism lesion is central-slip disruption/insufficiency with triangular-ligament attenuation and volar migration of the lateral bands; the lateral bands then act as PIP flexors, producing PIP flexion (often with secondary DIP hyperextension).

key_findings.finding: Dorsal repositioning of the lateral bands is the reconstructive maneuver associated with boutonnière correction, commonly combined with central-slip reconstruction/repair. In contrast, swan-neck reconstruction uses volar translocation of the lateral bands.
